question: Take out the kick and bass, add the snare roll, then bring them back. Did listeners' dopamine rise in the build or the drop?
answer: In both, in different places. Valorie Salimpoor's team scanned people hearing their favourite music: dopamine rose in the caudate while they anticipated the peak, and in the nucleus accumbens when the chill arrived. The build is a pleasure of its own: half the thrill is the wait.
move: Expectation is not the queue for pleasure; it is part of the pleasure.
ask: What am I rushing to get to, when looking forward to it is half the joy?

moments.name: The build
moments.text: No kick, no bass, a roll speeding up: the wait. Dopamine rose in the caudate.

moments.name: The drop
moments.text: Everything back. At the peak, dopamine came in another place, the accumbens.

reference: Salimpoor, Benovoy, Larcher, Dagher & Zatorre, Anatomically distinct dopamine release during anticipation and experience of peak emotion to music, Nature Neuroscience, 2011
